newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canada's Chretien backs joint French sales to Asia.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien backs joint French sales to Asia.

text.p: Visiting Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Thursday that France and Canada should launch joint economic projects aimed at increasing sales of consumer goods to Asia.

"If Asian countries which have huge populations become consumer-oriented, there will be much demand for Canadian and French products and, in certain circumstances, the possibility of joint projects between France and Canada," he said.
Chretien, who recently concluded a visit to the Far East, was speaking to reporters after meeting President Jacques Chirac on the final day of a three-day visit to France.

Chretien said he outlined his suggestion to French business leaders because "Asia and the Pacific are markets of the future for them too. The economic growth of Asia is as important to them as it is to us".

In talks with Chirac, and later with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, Chretien discussed a wide range of international issues including security in Europe, the reform of NATO and relations with Russia.
Presidential aides said both Chirac and Chretien called for an international peace conference to solve the problems of Africa's Great Lakes region.
